traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md defines a validation rule that must enforce format and syntax for @story and @req annotations (including path patterns, requirement ID patterns, multiline support, flexible parsing, and specific error messages), integrate with the existing plugin, and be documented and tested.
Evidence shows this is fully implemented: - The ESLint rule `src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts` is dedicated to validating `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` annotations. It uses shared helpers, a proper ESLint `meta` definition, schema, and messageIds. The implementation explicitly references this story and its requirements via annotations. - The test suite `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` is explicitly tagged as tests for this story and includes focused tests for each listed requirement (REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING, and detailed error messaging), covering both valid and invalid cases including edge cases and malformed comments. - Jest was run with `--verbose`; all tests, including the full valid-annotation-format suite, passed. - The rule documentation in `docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md` provides a clear format specification, configuration options, and examples of correct and incorrect annotations, matching the story’s documentation acceptance criterion.
Based on the implemented rule, comprehensive tests directly mapped to the story’s requirements, and supporting documentation, all acceptance criteria for this story are satisfied.
